title: A Dynamical Theory of Sequential Retrieval in Input-Driven Hopfield Networks
summary: Reasoning is the ability to integrate internal states and external inputs in a meaningful and semantically consistent flow. Contemporary machine learning (ML) systems increasingly rely on such sequential reasoning, from language understanding to multi-modal generation, often operating over dictionaries of prototypical patterns reminiscent of associative memory models. Understanding retrieval and sequentiality in associative memory models provides a powerful bridge to gain insight into ML reasoning.
